properties.description:
FICTIONAL - TRIAL MATERIAL. Made-up program, nation and radar.

KESTREL-ASSESS v1
Threat assessment: the KESTREL radar fielded by Varkos
Issued by: Intelligence organisation (Intel)
For: Project HARRIER acquisition team (RWR for a small reconnaissance UAV)
Date of issue: 2026-10-22
Information current to: the most recent observations, 2025
Supersedes: none (first issue)

KEY JUDGMENTS
KJ1 (HIGH confidence). The fielded KESTREL radar operates in the X band (8-12 GHz). Its emissions have been observed at 9.4 GHz.
KJ2 (LOW confidence, either way). We cannot determine whether the fielded KESTREL uses pulse-to-pulse frequency agility. A marketed variant, KESTREL-E, is advertised as agile across 8-12 GHz at more than 1,000 hops per second. Agility has not been observed in the fielded system, and the observations available do not exclude it.
KJ3 (MODERATE confidence). KESTREL's effective radiated power (ERP) is about 75 dBW. This is consistent with an antenna of about 1.2 m at X band (about 39 dBi gain) and a peak transmitter power of a few kilowatts.
KJ4 (MODERATE confidence). KESTREL uses a pulse-Doppler waveform with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of about 20 kHz. Other modes or PRFs may exist and have not been observed.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS
KA1. The emissions attributed to KESTREL come from KESTREL itself, not from another radar at the same site. (KJ3 and KJ4, and the 9.4 GHz observation in KJ1, rest on it. The X-band judgment in KJ1 does not.)
KA2. The fielded KESTREL has not been materially modified since the 2025 observations. (KJ3, KJ4.)
KA3. The ERP estimate reflects main-beam illumination. (KJ3.)
NOT ASSUMED. That the marketed variant KESTREL-E has the frequency capability of the fielded system. This is why KJ2 is unresolved.

CONFIDENCE LEVELS
HIGH: well corroborated by independent, reliable observation. MODERATE: credible but resting on a single line of observation or an estimate. LOW: the information is fragmentary or conflicting.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THESE JUDGMENTS
Observation of the fielded KESTREL's frequency over time would resolve KJ2. Evidence against KA1, KA2 or KA3 would lower KJ3 and KJ4.

NOTE FOR USERS
Because of KJ2, the single observed frequency (9.4 GHz) should not be read as the radar's only frequency.

HANDLING: releasable to the Project HARRIER acquisition team. Sources and methods are withheld.

properties.description: FICTIONAL. The release boundary between Intel and the Project HARRIER acquisition team: Intel publishes finished threat-assessment products about the KESTREL radar here; the acquisition team may rely on what is released and on nothing else. properties.error_model: A judgment found wrong is corrected by a new version that says what changed and why; a released version is never edited in place.
properties.name: KESTREL threat assessment release (Intel to HARRIER acquisition)
properties.operations: Intel: release a new version (supersedes the previous). Acquisition team: read and roll up the current version.
properties.payload_schema: A finished intelligence product, plain text: header (product id + version, date of issue, information currency, supersedes); KEY JUDGMENTS KJ1..KJn, each 'KJn (HIGH|MODERATE|LOW confidence). <judgment>'; KEY ASSUMPTIONS KA1..KAn, each naming the judgments that rest on it; CONFIDENCE LEVELS; WHAT WOULD CHANGE THESE JUDGMENTS; NOTE FOR USERS; HANDLING. The released text for each version is the Artifact that SPECIFIES this interface (art:kestrel-assess-v1 for v1), pinned by sha256.
properties.spec: Each release is one finished product with: product id and version (KESTREL-ASSESS vN); date of issue; information currency; KEY JUDGMENTS, each numbered (KJn) with a confidence level HIGH / MODERATE / LOW; KEY ASSUMPTIONS (KAn) and which judgments rest on each; confidence definitions; what would change the judgments; handling. Sources and methods are withheld. A new version supersedes the previous one and says so.
